sources.label: Boundaries
sources.text: Source: Survey of India, Government of India. 2020 Administrative Boundary Database (states and districts), metadata dated 16 October 2025. Two district names follow the official district directory (National Portal of India, 3 November 2026): Bengaluru South (formerly Rāmanagara) and Y.S.R. Kadapa. LGD codes: Local Government Directory, Ministry of Panchayati Raj (All Districts of India, 4 November 2026: 790 districts), matched by Census 2011 code, then by state and name for the districts formed after 2011
sources.credit: Source: Survey of India, Government of India

sources.label: Roads, railways, stations and rivers
sources.text: © OpenStreetMap contributors, under the ODbL 1.0; Geofabrik India extract. Roads are classed by their official number: national highways by MoRTH's list as on 31 December 2025 (Annual Report 2025-26, Appendix 2), NE numbers and motorways as expressways, SH numbers as state highways. Railways are the running lines (sidings, yards, spurs and crossovers left out), with narrow gauge. Station renamings from official notices (Hubballi: Press Information Bureau, 12 March 2023)

sources.label: Airports
sources.text: Official civil airports: eAIP India AD 1.3 and AD 1.4 (AIRAC November 2026), DGCA's licensed aerodromes (3 November 2026) and AAI's traffic statistics for October 2025 to September 2026 (Annexure III C). Scheduled flights means scheduled airline departures: DGCA’s Winter 2026 schedule could not be read (its files returned 404 on 3 November 2026), so an airport counts when AAI recorded at least 100 passengers in at least 3 of those 12 months, or in every month since it opened, except Juhu, HAL Bengaluru and Begumpet, whose traffic is business and general aviation only. Names are the eAIP's; where two airports serve one city, the others show their locality in brackets, for example Hyderabad International Airport (Begumpet). Coordinates and IATA codes: OurAirports (public domain, 2 November 2026). Size by AAI passengers, October 2025 to September 2026 (busy 5 million or more, medium 1 to 5 million, regional under 1 million); international as eAIP AD 1.3 lists them; flights a week from AAI's aircraft movements, July to September 2026 (Annexure II C)
sources.credit: Airports: AAI, DGCA; coordinates OurAirports (public domain)

sources.label: Population (District connectivity)
sources.text: GHS-POP R2023A, epoch 2025, 1 km grid (European Commission, Joint Research Centre; Schiavina et al. 2023, doi:10.2905/2FF68A52-5B5B-4A22-8F40-C41DA8332CFE; CC BY 4.0), the cells inside India's official outline. For each 1 km cell, the straight-line distance on the WGS 84 ellipsoid to the nearest national highway, railway station or halt, and airport with scheduled flights; per district, the share of people within 10 km, 10 km and 100 km of them, and the average of the three

items.status: DGCA's page lists the nine airlines' files (25 October 2026 to 27 March 2027), but every file returned 404. Until they can be read, scheduled flights follow AAI's monthly traffic, as the about page describes.

Left out of scheduled flights as business and general aviation only, by the owner's decision. No official statement says so; AAI's figures show about 3 passengers per aircraft movement, and the eAIP lists weekday operator hours and no customs or ground handling.

items.what: Seven small airports kept with scheduled flights
items.status: Mundra, Cooch-Behar, Jeypore, Jamshedpur, Rourkela, Utkela and Naini Saini (Pithoragarh) carry under 10 passengers per aircraft movement (AAI), as small 9- to 19-seat regional routes do. Nothing official says their traffic is business or general aviation only; DGCA's schedule would confirm it.

items.what: Darbhanga, Purnea and Ziro airports: names
items.status: Not in the eAIP or DGCA's licence lists (they appear only in AAI's traffic statistics, by place name), so their names are the place name with Airport; every other airport has its eAIP name.

items.what: Station names with a city's former name
items.status: Ahmadnagar (the city is Ahilyanagar since 13 March 2025), Gurgaon, Bangalore Cantonment and Shimoga Bidare keep their names: no official renaming of these stations was found, and Indian Railways' station list could not be read.
In the official district directory, but no official source found says which district or districts it was formed from, so the place card does not name an area for it.

notes.roads: Expressways 7,471 km · national highways 1,30,301 km · state highways 1,25,749 km; each road counted once, by its official number

railways.text: Running lines only, parallel tracks counted once. Indian Railways: 69,440 route km on 31 March 2025.

airports.text: Government count: 166 operational airports, including heliports and water aerodromes (Rajya Sabha, 27 July 2026). ARCS shows the 150 aeroplane airports, of which 130 have scheduled flights.
